turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same n-i-p (regular) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".

## Step 2: Key Device Physics Principles

**ETL considerations (n-i-p architecture):**
- TiO2-c (compact) is the workhorse blocking layer; adding a second functional layer (SnO2-np, PCBM-60, C60, BaSnO3-np, SnO2) improves electron extraction and reduces recombination at the ETL/perovskite interface
- SnO2-based ETLs have better band alignment with MAPbI3 (CBM ~−4.0 eV vs −3.9 eV for TiO2), lower trap density, and higher electron mobility
- PCBM-60/C60 interlayers passivate TiO2 surface traps and improve electron selectivity
- Bilayer ETLs (TiO2-c + functional interlayer) consistently outperform single-layer ETLs

**HTL considerations:**
- Spiro-MeOTAD remains the gold standard for n-i-p MAPbI3 (HOMO ~−5.1 eV, good match to MAPbI3 VBM ~−5.4 eV)
- PTAA is excellent (HOMO ~−5.1 eV, high hole mobility, hydrophobic = better stability)
- Novel HTMs (PCDTBT variants, TPA-based, PHPT-py) can exceed Spiro when well-matched
- Composite HTLs (PMMA|Spiro, PbS-QDs|Spiro, IEICO-4F|Spiro) add passivation
- P3HT is mediocre (~9–12% range typically)

**Back contact:**
- Au is the classic high-work-function contact (5.1 eV), excellent for Spiro-MeOTAD
- Ag works well with MoO3 interlayer (prevents corrosion, adjusts work function)
- MoO3|Au or MoO3|Ag are premium contacts

**Substrate:**
- SLG|FTO dominates high-efficiency devices; SLG|ITO also good
- Flexible substrates (PEN, PET) generally lower PCE

**Deposition:**
- Spin-coating is standard and reliable for MAPbI3
- Multi-step processes (>> CBD, >> Spin-coating) can improve morphology
- Co-evaporation gives very uniform films

## Step 3: Evaluate Each Candidate

Let me score each candidate systematically against the high-PCE patterns:

**c005** – SLG|ITO, TiO2-c|PCBM-60, PCDTBT8, MoO3|Au, Spin-coating>>Spin-coating
- Nearly identical to the 19.35% device (TiO2-c|PCBM-60, PCDTBT1, MoO3|Au). PCDTBT8 vs PCDTBT1 — both are PCDTBT variants with similar backbone, likely similar performance. Bilayer ETL with PCBM-60 passivation is excellent. MoO3|Au is a premium contact. ITO substrate is fine. **Very high potential: ~18–19%**

**c017** – SLG|ITO, C60;PhIm|C60, TaTM|F6-TCNNQ;TaTm, Ag, Co-evaporation
- Very similar to the 17.9% device (C60;Phlm|C60, TaTm|F6-TCNNQ;TaTm, Au, Co-evaporation). PhIm vs Phlm is likely the same compound (phenyl imidazole vs phenyl). Ag instead of Au — slightly lower work function but acceptable with this HTL stack. Co-evaporation gives excellent film uniformity. TaTm|F6-TCNNQ is a doped HTL with very high conductivity. **High potential: ~17–18%**

**c068** – SLG|ITO, SnO2-np|TiO2-np, PTAA, Au|MoO3, Spin-coating
- SnO2-np is excellent ETL. Adding TiO2-np creates a bilayer with complementary band alignment. PTAA is a top-tier HTL (18.19% with SnO2-np|PTAA|Ag). Au|MoO3 is an unusual contact order (MoO3 usually goes between HTL and metal), but if it means Au with MoO3 interlayer, it's fine. PTAA + SnO2 bilayer is a strong combination. **High potential: ~17–18%**

**c073** – SLG|ITO-HMDS Scaffold, TiO2-c|C60, PTAA, Ag, Spin-coating
- TiO2-c|C60 ETL (similar to 17.2% device with TiO2-c|C60|Spiro-MeOTAD|Ag). PTAA instead of Spiro — PTAA is excellent. ITO-HMDS scaffold substrate is unusual but ITO-based. C60 as ETL interlayer passivates TiO2 surface. PTAA|Ag is a good combination. **High potential: ~16–17%**

**c045** – SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-nanofibers, PTAA, Au, Spin-coating
- TiO2-c|TiO2-nanofibers ETL: nanofibers provide high surface area and good electron transport. PTAA is excellent HTL. Au back contact. FTO substrate. Training data shows TiO2-c|TiO2-nanofibres|Spiro-MeOTAD|Au = 12.06%, but PTAA is significantly better than Spiro in many configurations. The 18.9% device uses TiO2-c|BaSnO3-np|PTAA|Au. PTAA+Au is a premium combination. **Moderate-high: ~15–17%**

**c064** – SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|SnO2-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
- TiO2-c|SnO2-np is the same ETL as the 20.85% device! That device used Ag + Dipp-coating. Here we have Au + Spin-coating. Au is slightly better work function match. Spin-coating is standard. The 17.47% device uses TiO2-c|SnO2|Spiro-MeOTAD|Ag. This configuration is very close to top performers. **Very high potential: ~18–20%**

**c025** – SLG|FTO, SnO2-c|TiO2-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, Ag, Spin-coating>>CBD
- SnO2-c compact layer + TiO2-np. SnO2-c alone gives 14.72% with Spiro/Au. Adding TiO2-np interlayer should improve. Ag back contact. CBD step helps morphology. Training: SnO2-c|TiO2-c = 16.54%. This is similar. **Moderate-high: ~15–17%**

**c021** – PEN|ITO, SnO2-np|CPTA, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
- Flexible substrate (PEN) limits PCE. CPTA is a SAM/passivation agent for SnO2. SnO2-np is excellent. But PEN substrate typically gives ~11–13%. **Moderate: ~13–15%**

**c031** – SLG|FTO, SnO2-c|SnO2-mp|TiO2-c, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
- Triple ETL stack. SnO2-c|SnO2-mp|TiO2-c is complex. Training shows SnO2-c|TiO2-c = 16.54%. Adding SnO2-mp mesoporous layer could help or hurt (more interfaces = more recombination risk). Spiro-MeOTAD|Au is standard. **Moderate-high: ~15–17%**

**c080** – SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|MPMIC60, Spiro-MeOTAD, Ag, Spin-coating
- MPMIC60 is a fullerene derivative (methano[60]fullerene) used as ETL interlayer/passivation. Similar to PCBM-60 interlayer. TiO2-c|PCBM-60|Spiro-MeOTAD|Ag = 14.25% in training. MPMIC60 is a more functionalized fullerene, potentially better passivation. **Moderate-high: ~15–17%**

**c013** – SLG|FTO, TiO2-c, P(VDF-TrFE)|Spiro-MeOTAD, MoO3|Ag, Spin-coating
- P(VDF-TrFE) is a ferroelectric polymer used as interlayer between perovskite and Spiro. Can improve charge extraction via built-in field. MoO3|Ag is a good contact. TiO2-c single layer ETL. Training: TiO2-c|IEICO-4F|Spiro-MeOTAD|MoO3|Ag = 18.965%. The ferroelectric interlayer concept is promising. **Moderate-high: ~15–17%**

**c055** – SLG|ITO, TiO2-c, PTB7, Au, Spin-coating
- PTB7 is a polymer HTL. Training: TiO2-c|TiO2-mp|PTB7|Ag = 12.65%. Single TiO2-c ETL. PTB7 is decent but not top-tier. **Moderate: ~13–15%**

**c046** – SLG|FTO, TiO2-c, ITIC, Au, Spin-coating
- ITIC is a non-fullerene acceptor used as HTL. Novel but not well-established as HTL. TiO2-c single ETL. **Uncertain, likely moderate: ~12–15%**

**c083** – SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|Dimethylbiguanide, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
- Dimethylbiguanide (metformin) as ETL additive/interlayer. Can passivate TiO2 surface traps. Spiro-MeOTAD|Au is standard. Similar to TiO2-c|modifier|Spiro|Au configurations (~15–17%). **Moderate-high: ~15–16%**

**c086** – SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|AAO, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Drop-infiltration>>Spin-coating
- Training: TiO2-c|AAO|Spiro-MeOTAD|MoOx|ITO = 7.5%. The AAO (anodic aluminum oxide) template approach with drop-infiltration is less efficient. Au instead of MoOx|ITO might help slightly but the architecture is limiting. **Low-moderate: ~8–10%**

**c010** – SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, 2TPA-2-DP, Au, Spin-coating>>CBD
- 2TPA-2-DP is a TPA-based HTM. TPA-BPFN-TPA gives 18.4% with TiO2-c|TiO2-mp|Ag. 2TPA-2-DP is a different TPA derivative. TiO2-c|TiO2-mp ETL is standard. Au back contact. CBD step. **High potential: ~15–18%**

**c047** – SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, FU7, Au, Spin-coating

- BT41 is a novel HTM. Similar pattern. **Moderate-high: ~14–16%**

- S5 is a novel HTM. **Moderate-high: ~14–16%**

- TSHBC is a novel HTM (likely a triphenylamine or carbazole derivative). CBD step. **Moderate-high: ~14–16%**

**c098** – SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, PyThTPA, Au, Spin-coating
- PyThTPA is a TPA-based HTM with pyridine-thiophene units. TPA-based HTMs have shown excellent performance (TPA-BPFN-TPA = 18.4%). **High potential: ~16–18%**

**c040** – SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, 3,6-cbz-EDOT, Au, Spin-coating>>Spin-coating>>Spin-coating
- Carbazole-EDOT HTM. Three spin-coating steps suggests careful layer-by-layer deposition. **Moderate-high: ~14–16%**

**c041** – SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, TT80, Au, Spin-coating>>CBD
- TT80 is a novel HTM. CBD step. **Moderate-high: ~14–16%**

**c043** – SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, DAHI|Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
- DAHI as interlayer + Spiro-MeOTAD. Composite HTL approach. Training: PMMA|Spiro = 18.01%, Graphene oxide|Spiro = 16.15%. DAHI (likely a passivating agent) + Spiro could be good. **Moderate-high: ~15–17%**

**c078** – SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|Al2O3-mp|NiO-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating

**c089** – SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp|Al2O3-mp, NiO-mp, Carbon, Drop-infiltration>>CBD
- Training: TiO2-c|TiO2-mp|Al2O3-mp|NiO-mp|Spiro-MeOTAD|Au = 16.32%, and TiO2-c|TiO2-mp|ZrO2-mp|NiO-mp|Carbon = 13.5% (Dropcasting>>CBD). This uses NiO-mp HTL with Carbon back contact. Carbon back contacts limit PCE. **Moderate: ~13–15%**

**c058** – SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp|ZrO2-mp, NiO-np, Carbon, Drop-infiltration
- Training: TiO2-c|TiO2-mp|ZrO2-mp|NiO-mp|Carbon = 9.35% (Drop-infiltration) and 13.5% (Dropcasting>>CBD). NiO-np vs NiO-mp. Carbon back contact limits. **Moderate: ~10–14%**

- Training: TiO2-c|Al2O3-mp|Spiro-MeOTAD|Ag = 9.42%, TiO2-c|Al2O3-mp|Spiro-MeOTAD|Ag = 10.1%. Al2O3-c (compact) vs Al2O3-mp. Ag|Au bilayer contact. **Moderate: ~12–15%**

**c061** – SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|WO3, Spiro-MeOTAD, Ag, Spin-coating>>Spin-coating

**c024** – SLG|FTO, WO3, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating>>Gas reaction

**c030** – SLG|ITO, C60, IDF-SFXPh|MoO3, Ag, Spin-coating
- C60 ETL (training: C60|Spiro-MeOTAD|Au = 12.11%, C60|Spiro-MeOTAD|MoO3|Ag = 15.05%). IDF-SFXPh is a novel HTM. MoO3 interlayer before Ag. **Moderate-high: ~14–16%**

- Training: C60|Spiro-MeOTAD|MoO3|Ag = 15.05% (FTO), C60|Spiro-MeOTAD|Au = 12.11% (FTO). ITO substrate, Ag without MoO3. **Moderate: ~13–15%**

**c099** – SLG|ITO, TiO2-c|PNP, Spiro-MeOTAD, Ag, Spin-coating

## Step 4: Final Ranking of Top Candidates

Based on the analysis, my top candidates are:

1. **c064** – SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|SnO2-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
   - The TiO2-c|SnO2-np ETL is identical to the highest-performing training device (20.85%). SnO2-np provides superior electron mobility and better band alignment than TiO2 alone. The bilayer creates an excellent electron-selective contact. Spiro-MeOTAD|Au is the gold-standard HTL/contact combination. Spin-coating on FTO is the most reproducible process. Expected: **~18–20%**

2. **c005** – SLG|ITO, TiO2-c|PCBM-60, PCDTBT8, MoO3|Au, Spin-coating>>Spin-coating
   - Nearly identical to the 19.35% training device (PCDTBT1 → PCDTBT8, same backbone family). TiO2-c|PCBM-60 ETL passivates TiO2 traps. PCDTBT is a high-performance polymer HTM. MoO3|Au is an excellent ohmic contact. Expected: **~17–19%**

3. **c017** – SLG|ITO, C60;PhIm|C60, TaTM|F6-TCNNQ;TaTm, Ag, Co-evaporation
   - Near-identical to the 17.9% training device. Doped TaTm HTL with F6-TCNNQ provides very high conductivity and excellent hole extraction. Co-evaporation gives pinhole-free films. Expected: **~17–18%**

4. **c068** – SLG|ITO, SnO2-np|TiO2-np, PTAA, Au|MoO3, Spin-coating
   - SnO2-np|TiO2-np bilayer ETL combines the best of both oxides. PTAA is a top-tier HTL (18.19% with SnO2-np|PTAA|Ag in training). Au|MoO3 contact. Expected: **~16–18%**

5. **c098** – SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, PyThTPA, Au, Spin-coating
   - PyThTPA is a TPA-based HTM with pyridine-thiophene units, structurally related to TPA-BPFN-TPA (18.4% in training). TiO2-c|TiO2-mp is a well-established ETL. Au back contact. TPA-based HTMs consistently outperform Spiro in this dataset. Expected: **~16–18%**

Honorable mentions: c073 (TiO2-c|C60|PTAA|Ag, ~16–17%), c045 (TiO2-c|TiO2-nanofibers|PTAA|Au, ~15–17%), c010 (TiO2-c|TiO2-mp|2TPA-2-DP|Au, ~15–17%)
